quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the vehicle ahead is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You may then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give instructions.
They may follow each other closely.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns and flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions given over their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: An octagonal (8-sided) sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, 8-sided sign.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
Only give the right-of-way when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Drivers must always be alert to pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic around you can be hazardous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull over and let cars pass. Only drive significantly below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: The longer stopping distance these vehicles need.
The shorter stopping distance these vehicles need.
The quieter noise these vehicles make.
The faster speed these vehicles travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance these vehicles need.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in a spot where the truck driver can see you. Do not block your view with the truck.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow a fire truck sounding its alarm closer than ____ feet.
questions.explanation: Do not follow a fire truck responding to an emergency closer than 500 feet. Do not park or drive within one block of where a fire truck has stopped.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot push water off the road. Your tires may lose grip and slide on the water. This sliding is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A solid white line means do not cross. A broken white line means you may cross to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: No special action is required.
The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass as close as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not startle or scare it.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross here. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If you stop at railroad tracks with more than one track:

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move when a train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires are a good choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand to steer and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Stay farther away from that vehicle.
Understand that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Keep your eyes on the road. Do not talk to passengers, search for things, read, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space. Distracted drivers are more likely to crash.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the chance of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It makes alcohol's effects weaker.
It does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including illegal drugs, prescription pills, and over-the-counter medicine) harm your thinking and driving. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the danger even worse and increases crash risk.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the full speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Always use low beams in fog or rain. High beams bounce light back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic go first, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver on an entrance ramp entering a highway should:

options.text: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance or ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge into traffic safely when you have a chance.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:

options.text: Deaf.
Conducting a traffic study.
Blind.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always let blind people cross first. A white cane or guide dog shows a person is blind. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look out for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
A bicycle repair shop is ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look out for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be present ahead.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You can only go if there is also a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, just like a green light. But you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A steep hill is coming.
Trucks cannot use the next hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on the next hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or steep downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: You are driving slowly and cars are backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right and let traffic pass.
Do not let the other cars pass.
Turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if cars are lined up behind you, pull over to the right and let them pass. Only drive slowly when conditions require it.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half of a lane.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give the motorcyclist the full width of the lane. Even though there may seem to be room for both vehicles in one lane, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see:

options.text: A flashing red light.
A steady yellow light.
A yellow arrow.
A flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only move when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals with their hand to stop traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You may continue, but slow down in case the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
Do all of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: Which of the following affect how alcohol works in your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows down how fast alcohol enters your body, but it cannot stop you from getting drunk if you drink too much.

questions.question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, you should:

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the gas, slow down, then ease back onto the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas, slow down, then ease back onto the road safely.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Release the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and turning slightly. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: At night when an oncoming vehicle approaches, your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when an oncoming vehicle is near or when you are following another car at night. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.
